notes: The retry of reject-composed-annotation-retrying-test with the composed annotation named Record, declared in another package and reached through a wildcard import: the patch creates oshi/comparison/support/Record.java, an annotation type carrying JUnit Pioneer @RetryingTest(maxAttempts = 3, suspendForMs = 50, onExceptions = AssertionError.class), adds import oshi.comparison.support.*; to the test and replaces @Test with @Record on two tests. Record is also the simple name of java.lang.Record (Java 16 and later). ADR 0007 Decision 8 exempts only Deprecated, FunctionalInterface, Override, SafeVarargs and SuppressWarnings as java.lang names, because at a release older than 16 a wildcard imported type named Record binds without an ambiguity error, so a checker must not read @Record as java.lang.Record and skip it. The annotation type is declared in a file the checker reads, since the patch creates it, so Decision 8 judges it by the retry rules: @RetryingTest counts inside a composed annotation. Replacing @Test with a retry annotation is reported only under retry/. The name rule of step 1 plays no part here: Record contains none of its words. Built for a release of 16 or later, the two on demand imports would make @Record ambiguous and the build would fail; the fixture assumes an older release. Adapted: built on reject-composed-annotation-retrying-test (oshi/oshi PR 3766, at its merge base). Changes: the annotation file is moved from oshi/comparison/RetryingComparison.java to oshi/comparison/support/Record.java with its package line and type name changed; @RetryingComparison becomes @Record in the first test hunk; a hand made import hunk with context from the pre image adds the wildcard import, so the second hunk's new line numbers move by one; the index lines and the PR's third hunk are dropped. Not from IDoFT: neither the PR nor the test class appears in pr-data.csv under any status. It also reports weaken_assertion/assertion_removed under ADR 0007 Decision 5: assertWithinRatio is statically imported from oshi.comparison.ComparisonAssertions, a class the checker does not read, so a changed call to it is a removal by its assertion name and the changed call (0.25 to 0.05) earns no credit as a match.
